claim_scope: The shared Python canonical byte encoder derives both its length prefix and payload from one snapshot of the caller-supplied bytes or bytearray buffer, without dispatching a subclass __bytes__ hook.
failure_modes: a bytes subclass replaces the raw buffer through __bytes__ before hashing or signing
a bytearray subclass replaces the raw buffer through __bytes__ before hashing or signing
the canonical length prefix authenticates attacker-selected replacement bytes instead of the supplied buffer

aaa.reason: The regression arranges bytes and bytearray subclasses whose raw buffers disagree with their hostile __bytes__ results, acts through encode_bytes, and asserts exact length-prefixed raw-buffer encodings.

reject_is_noop.reason: The reproduced defect concerns accepted bytes-like values and pure canonical output. Existing type rejection remains unchanged and the helper has no mutable state.

mutations.description: copy accepted bytes-like values with bytes(value), dispatching attacker-controlled __bytes__
derive the prefix or payload from the hostile replacement instead of the raw buffer

nonclaims: This packet establishes one Python canonical-encoding boundary regression; it is not a proof of every caller or cross-language codec.
Canonical outputs for ordinary exact bytes and bytearray inputs remain unchanged.
No proof, release, runtime, settlement, migration, writer-rotation, or production authority is granted; production_authority remains NONE.
